technical.lead: Agent-security funding and a live Claude Cowork sandbox escape land in one week
technical.body: The AI-agent runtime is hardening into its own attack surface with a funded defensive market forming around it. Straiker, pitching itself as the agentic-security company, closed a $64 million Series A led by Marathon Management Partners with Citi Ventures, Illuminate Financial, and Workday Ventures, lifting its total to $85 million and claiming run-rate revenue up more than 15x in under a year, per SiliconANGLE and Straiker's own announcement. Its platform spans Discover AI (finding agents and their tool access), Ascend AI (pre-deployment red-teaming), and Defend AI (runtime guardrails). The same week, researchers at Armadin detailed a full sandbox-escape chain in Anthropic's Claude Cowork that reaches root inside the isolated Ubuntu VM by abusing a resume flag that skips unprivileged-user creation and a domain-override that disables the network allowlist, per SiliconANGLE and Cybersecurity News. Anthropic shipped a June 30 patch tightening namespace boundaries, seccomp profiles, and Linux capabilities while disputing it as a security issue since exploitation presumes existing host access. The through-line: the agent sandbox is now both a live vulnerability class and a funded product category.

technical.lead: Koduri's Oxmiq raises $35M to license an AI GPU architecture, adds Keller
technical.body: Oxmiq Labs, founded by former Intel and AMD graphics chief Raja Koduri, closed a $35 million Series A that brings its total to $60 million, led by the Samsung Catalyst Fund and Fundomo with MediaTek, Pegatron Venture Capital, and others participating, per SiliconANGLE. Rather than fabricating accelerators, Oxmiq commercializes OxCore, a licensable GPU architecture folding graphics, CPU, and tensor-accelerator roles into one design a chipmaker can build a custom AI processor on without a ground-up chip program, per the company's release. Koduri frames the ambition as becoming the Arm of the AI-silicon era, licensing the foundation instead of competing SKU-for-SKU with NVIDIA and AMD. The signal it is more than a slide deck is the board addition of Jim Keller, the Tenstorrent CEO behind some of the industry's most consequential architectures, per The Next Web. For buyers watching the non-NVIDIA field, the competitive layer is moving upstream from finished parts to the IP that lets any system builder spin its own.

technical.lead: Unsloth ships DeepSeek-V4 fine-tuning as the 1.6T model graduates from preview
technical.body: Unsloth added DeepSeek-V4 support with all reasoning levels enabled in its Studio build tagged July 7, 2026, per the Unsloth changelog, extending the fine-tuning stack to the largest open-weight family it now covers alongside GLM-5.2 and MiniMax-M3. The timing tracks DeepSeek-V4's own trajectory: the Pro and Flash variants, a 1.6-trillion-parameter MoE with roughly 49 billion active parameters and a one-million-token context plus a 284-billion-parameter sibling, first shipped in April as an MIT-licensed preview and are now moving to an official mid-July release with refined pricing, per MindStudio and DeepSeek's API documentation. An open-weight model at that scale is only practically useful to most teams if a tuning path exists that does not require a full training cluster, and Unsloth's pitch is cutting the VRAM and time cost of adapting these models on commodity hardware. With serving also converging (DeepSeek-V4 endorses SGLang and vLLM for inference), the download-tune-serve loop for a genuine frontier-tier Chinese model is now a same-week, off-the-shelf pipeline.

technical.lead: OpenAI ships gpt-realtime-2.1 and lines up a three-tier GPT-5.6 lineup
technical.body: OpenAI released gpt-realtime-2.1 and a smaller gpt-realtime-2.1-mini on July 6, 2026, advertising at least 25 percent lower p95 latency across its realtime voice models along with better alphanumeric recognition, silence and noise handling, and interruption behavior, with the mini tier priced well below the full model to widen access for speech-to-speech agents, per OpenAI's release notes. In parallel, OpenAI opened a limited preview of GPT-5.6 to a small set of trusted partners, a three-model family named Sol, Terra, and Luna with published per-million-token pricing of $5/$30, $2.50/$15, and $1/$6 respectively and a broader rollout promised in the coming weeks, per the same notes and reporting collected by LLM-Stats. The pattern across both moves is a deliberate push down the cost curve and toward operational deployment rather than raw capability headlines: a tiered lineup letting builders pick a cheaper Luna or Terra tier for high-volume work, and a realtime update explicitly tuned for voice-agent workflows. For teams weighing hosted frontier APIs against self-hosted open weights, the closed-model side is now competing on latency and price-per-tier, the same axes the open-weight serving stacks have been arguing.

technical.lead: AI events to plan around: ICML in Seoul, AI Tinkerers SF, UN talks in Geneva
technical.body: The live research item this week is ICML 2026 in Seoul, with the main conference July 7-9 and workshops July 10-11 at COEX. For Bay Area locals, AI Tinkerers San Francisco hosts its next meetup July 8, a go-to-market engineering track in the usual three-hour working-demo format. On governance, the UN's first Global Dialogue on AI Governance convenes all 193 member states in Geneva on July 6-7 at Palexpo, alongside the ITU AI for Good summit, with the new Independent International Scientific Panel on AI presenting a preliminary report. On the chip track, AMD's MI400 Instinct series and Helios rack-scale system remain the marquee second-half-2026 catalyst, while the nearest confirmed hardware gathering is Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford on August 23-25 (early registration closes July 31), followed by the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17. The AI-security block clusters in early-to-mid August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas in early August, and OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6. On the enterprise track, Ai4 2026 runs August 4-6 at The Venetian in Las Vegas, GitHub Universe is October 28-29, and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4. The two immediate actions: catch the ICML program through July 11 if research is your beat, and the July 8 AI Tinkerers SF meetup if you are local.
